correctness.rationale: Each nonzero decomposable tensor is on one of (q+1)^3 projective Segre points, each scalar class summed by character orthogonality. A two-slice representation gives F(T)=q(q B(T)-q-2), with B the number of hyperbolic quadric Q=P1xP1 points in the projective common kernel. Rank-two slice pairs correspond to all P3 lines with multiplicity |GL2(q)|; the quadric has 2(q+1) contained generators, (q+1)^2(q-1) tangents, q^2(q+1)^2/2 secants and q^2(q-1)^2/2 external lines. Rank-one slices correspond to tangent or non-tangent hyperplane sections, and rank zero contributes T=0; these disjoint cases sum to q^8. The six signed values are q(qB-q-2), hence only B=0 and B=1 negative, and B=2 vanishes only at q=2. Fourier inversion gives the exact convolution ℓ1 and ℓ∞ norms by the absolute kernel sum. The general all-prime-power conclusion follows combinatorial counting, not the finite q tests. Independently checked q=2 by complete 256-input integer Walsh transform: 108 zeros and norm 55/16.
